goal: Fix the reproduced defect (run_id 20260907T193310Z-f6a756d2) where real_claude_builder_invoker() discards a real, valid, resumable session_id whenever the inner structured builder result fails extraction (Claude finished real work but replied in prose instead of the required JSON object) -- forcing every retry to start a brand-new session with no memory of already-completed work. Make the smallest reliable change so a builder invocation with a successfully-parsed outer provider envelope, a trustworthy session_id, but a failed inner-result extraction preserves that session identity (via a new RecoverableSessionInfrastructureError carrying session_id) and performs a bounded resumed retry with a narrow, completion-focused instruction aimed at finishing already-started work and emitting the required structured completion result -- never blindly rerunning the full original task. Do not weaken fail-closed structured-result validation. Do not redesign the controller.
acceptance_conditions: A new RecoverableSessionInfrastructureError (subclass of InfrastructureError) carries a session_id and is raised ONLY when the outer provider envelope parsed as strict JSON, was a mapping, and carried a trustworthy non-empty string session_id, but the inner structured result failed extract_schema_valid_result().

A malformed/unparseable outer envelope, a non-mapping envelope, or an envelope with no trustworthy string session_id, never raises the recoverable subtype -- remains plain InfrastructureError, unchanged.

The manifest's builder_session_id is persisted from a RecoverableSessionInfrastructureError's session_id even though the overall invocation still fails closed (self-loop retry, bounded by the existing infrastructure_retry_limit, unchanged).
The very next builder retry after a recoverable failure passes that exact recovered session_id to the builder adapter, which threads it into --resume <session_id> in the real CLI invocation.

That resumed retry uses a narrow, completion-focused prompt distinct from the full original task prompt -- it must not authorize broader/new work and must not blindly restate the full goal/allowed_paths/forbidden_paths as if reissuing the whole task.
A successful resumed retry transitions normally onward (BUILDING/REPAIRING/CORRECTING_REVIEW -> TESTING) exactly like any other successful builder result.
An invalid inner result is never treated as success merely because in-scope files already changed in the working tree.
Two or more conflicting schema-valid inner result candidates still fail closed (ambiguous), and remain recoverable only if a trustworthy session_id accompanies them.
Normal first-attempt builder behavior (session_id=None, full original task prompt) is unchanged.

REPAIRING and CORRECTING_REVIEW's existing session-threading and full-prompt behavior (for a session established by a genuinely successful builder turn) is unchanged and not confused with the new narrow recovery path.
No new top-level manifest field is added (schemas/milestone_run.schema.json is out of scope for this milestone); recovery-pending state is derived from the run's own local events.jsonl.

SR-CRASH-1 (Cursor correction): a process crash between the durable BUILDER_SESSION_RECOVERED event write and the durable manifest save is tolerated -- the next advance() reconstructs the exact pending session_id purely from events.jsonl (never depends on any single in-memory or manifest write having completed), self-heals the manifest field, and uses it for both the invocation and the narrow resumed-completion prompt.

A stale BUILDER_SESSION_RECOVERED event followed by a genuine BUILDER_INVOKED event never resurrects as pending recovery on a later advance(); of multiple recovery events without an intervening invocation, only the latest still-pending one governs.

SR-WS-1 (Cursor correction): a recoverable session_id must satisfy isinstance(value, str) and value.strip() non-empty; the STRIPPED canonical value is what is persisted and carried into --resume. Whitespace-only, empty, absent/None, and non-string session_id forms all remain plain, non-recoverable InfrastructureError.
